title: Energy Balance and Metabolism

sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Think of your body like a phone that uses battery all day. TDEE is the total battery you drain from morning to night, added up from everything: the background apps always running (basal metabolism), digesting food, and moving around. The other terms are just single apps, not the full total.

### Question 2

Even when you are lying totally still doing nothing, your heart beats, your lungs breathe, and your cells keep working. BMR is the fuel needed just to stay alive and 'idling,' like a car engine running while parked. It is the biggest chunk of energy most people use each day.

### Question 3

Imagine a bank account where the money you put in matches the money you spend. Your balance stays the same. With energy, when the calories you eat match the calories you burn, your weight holds steady. That perfect match is called energy balance.

### Question 4

Muscle is like a hungry, always-on machine, while fat is more like a quiet storage box. Even when you sit still, muscle keeps asking for fuel to stay ready. So the more muscle you carry, the more calories you burn just resting.

### Question 5

Digesting food usually takes about the same small slice of the calories you eat, roughly a tenth, so as a share of your day it does not swing much. (Protein costs a bit more to digest than carbs or fat.) But how much you move around, from lying on the couch to running errands all day, can change a lot day to day. That is why exercise is the part you can most easily change.

### Question 6

If you keep putting more into a backpack than you take out, it gets heavier. When you eat more energy than you use, your body tucks the extra away, mostly as fat, so your weight slowly climbs. That extra-in situation is called positive energy balance.

### Question 7

Your energy burn goes down when you have less muscle (the hungry engine gets smaller) and when you barely move. Both shrink the calories you use. Sitting still all day with less muscle is like turning down the dial on your whole energy budget.

### Question 8

Two backpacks can weigh the same but be packed very differently. If one person's weight is mostly muscle and they move a lot, their body burns more fuel than someone the same weight with less muscle who sits around. Same number on the scale, different energy needs.

### Question 9

If you spend more money than you earn, your savings shrink. Burning more calories than you eat makes your body dip into its stored fuel, so weight goes down. Exercising more and eating a bit less is the classic recipe for that 'spending more than you earn' state.

### Question 10

Your body's 'always-on' systems, like your brain thinking and heart beating, never take a break, so they quietly use most of your energy every day. That baseline is your basal metabolic rate, and because it runs 24/7, it is usually the biggest slice of the energy pie.

### Question 11

When food gets scarce for a long time, your body acts like a phone switching to low-power mode to save battery. It burns fuel more slowly to hang on to what it has. That energy-saving slowdown is called adaptive thermogenesis, and it makes losing more weight harder.

### Question 12

Think of a savings account. When you earn more than you spend (positive balance), money piles up in savings. When you spend more than you earn (negative balance), you pull from savings. Your body does the same with energy, storing the extra or dipping into its fat reserves.
